english: Consider all ellipses $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$, $a>b>0$, that pass through the point $(4,3)$. For such an ellipse, let $A$ be an end of its major axis and $B$ an end of its minor axis. Among these ellipses, let $E_0$ be the one for which the length $AB$ is the least, and let $d$ be the distance between the foci of $E_0$. Then the value of $d^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: बिन्दु $(4,3)$ से होकर जाने वाले सभी दीर्घवृत्तों $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$, $a>b>0$, पर विचार कीजिए। ऐसे किसी दीर्घवृत्त के लिए, माना $A$ उसके दीर्घ अक्ष का एक अन्त्य बिन्दु तथा $B$ उसके लघु अक्ष का एक अन्त्य बिन्दु है। इन दीर्घवृत्तों में से माना $E_0$ वह है जिसके लिए लम्बाई $AB$ न्यूनतम है, तथा $d$ दीर्घवृत्त $E_0$ की नाभियों के बीच की दूरी है। तब $d^{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: $A(\pm a,0)$ and $B(0,\pm b)$, so $AB^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}$ for every choice of the ends. Minimising $AB$ is the same as minimising $a^{2}+b^{2}$.

By AM-GM, $\dfrac{16b^{2}}{a^{2}}+\dfrac{9a^{2}}{b^{2}}\ge2\sqrt{16\cdot9}=24$, so $a^{2}+b^{2}\ge49$, with equality when $\dfrac{16b^{2}}{a^{2}}=\dfrac{9a^{2}}{b^{2}}$, i.e. $\dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}=\dfrac34$.

Then $\dfrac{9}{b^{2}}=\dfrac{12}{a^{2}}$ and $\dfrac{28}{a^{2}}=1$: $a^{2}=28$, $b^{2}=21$. Since $b^{2}<a^{2}$, this ellipse belongs to the family, so $E_0:\ \dfrac{x^{2}}{28}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{21}=1$ with $AB=7$.
For $E_0$: $a^{2}e^{2}=a^{2}-b^{2}=7$, the foci are $(\pm\sqrt7,0)$ and $d=2\sqrt7$, so $d^{2}=28$ (and $e=\dfrac12$).
originality_note: New: the least distance between the ends of the two axes over the ellipses through a fixed point, done by multiplying by the constraint and AM-GM, then read off the foci (way 5). Closest known: least area pi ab of an ellipse through a fixed point (AM-GM on 2hk/ab). Different because: the quantity is a^2 + b^2, the bound is (4 + 3)^2 and the equality case must be checked against a > b before the foci are found.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, point and curve introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that the minimising ellipse satisfies a > b (b^2/a^2 = 3/4) and that AB is the same for every choice of ends. Changed: No change.
key_step: Write a^2 + b^2 = (a^2 + b^2)(16/a^2 + 9/b^2) and apply AM-GM; equality gives b^2/a^2 = 3/4.
justification: Two ideas linked: the constrained AM-GM (multiply by the constraint) and the elements of the ellipse (axis ends, foci) with an equality check; numerical answer. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q13 (L3), a numerical conic question linking foci and axes.

concept_use.Basic elements of the standard ellipse:: The ends of the major and minor axes give AB^2 = a^2 + b^2, and the foci of the optimal ellipse give d^2 = 4(a^2 - b^2) = 28.
concept_use.Arithmetic Mean (AM), Geometric Mean (GM: AM-GM on 16b^2/a^2 + 9a^2/b^2 after multiplying by the constraint 16/a^2 + 9/b^2 = 1 gives the minimum 49 and the equality case b^2/a^2 = 3/4.
